limitations.wanted: A shouldered axle pin (or a shoulder bolt) plus a thin spacer, to clamp the bearings' inner rings without any part of the mount touching the wheel
limitations.blocked_by: Not in the hardware list — only plain socket screws, hex/lock nuts, plain washers, heat-set inserts and a salvaged 1/4-20 bolt are available (no shoulder bolts, no spacers/shims, no retaining rings)
limitations.why: A plain bolt's Ø13 head and a nut's hex corners can rub the bearing's shield, and a flat hanger plate would otherwise squeeze the wheel's plastic and stop it turning; with no spacer on hand I had to make the 2 mm retaining lip deep enough that the 1.6 mm washer and the nut can reach inside it to the inner ring

limitations.wanted: PETG, ASA or nylon for the roller (or at least a filament with better creep and press-fit behaviour than PLA)
limitations.blocked_by: Only black high-speed PLA is listed in the available setup
limitations.why: The wheel carries a static door load for years and holds a press-fitted bearing; PLA creeps under sustained load and its press fit relaxes with time and warmth, so the bearing seat may loosen (a drop of superglue is the mitigation I wrote into the manual)

limitations.wanted: Measurements of the broken wheel's tread profile, the rail it ran on, and the hanger plate the axle goes through
limitations.blocked_by: The owner couldn't measure those parts (only the bolt's shank, ~8 mm) and the wheel had already snapped
limitations.why: Those three dimensions decide whether the tread needs a groove or should be plain, how wide the wheel must be to sit on the rail, and how long the axle assembly can be; without them I had to make the tread plain (works on both a flat bar and a rib) and design an axle stack that tolerates an unknown hanger thickness
